name: Teams
author: Smart Terminal
summary: Deliver a message to somebody in Microsoft Teams — for any extension that has something worth saying.
description: A delivery extension. It knows nothing about pull requests, builds or clusters: it takes a person, a few lines and some links, and gets them to Teams. Anything in this app may ask it to deliver, and the first time something new asks it stops and shows you what it wants to say, with a switch of its own from then on. Two ways out, both at once, and the screen says what each costs rather than making you pick one: a channel takes an Incoming Webhook — two minutes and no administrator — and posts where everybody reads it, with more rooms added by name so a sender can ask for the right one; a person is reached privately through an app registration with an administrator's consent, or the Code Reviewer's bot. A message for a room goes to the room and a message for somebody goes to them, never one in place of the other, and you can write to either or both yourself from its Send screen. A panel in this app cannot reach the network at all, so the credentials live in the app itself and no extension that sends through this one is ever told a tenant, a token or an address. What protects the person on the other end lives here too: the hours it may send in, at most one message per person per day whoever is asking, a ceiling for each extension so a loop in one cannot spend everybody's attention, and a key from the sender so the same thing is never said twice. Everything that went out is listed with what became of it, and a message that failed says why rather than disappearing.
